subject: Stolen Cannons of the American Revolution
overview: Host Laura Duggan interviewed author and historian John Bell about his book, 'The Road to Concord.' The discussion explored how the British search for four stolen brass cannons ultimately sparked the onset of the American Revolution.

items.title: Introduction of Guest John Bell
items.summary: Host Laura Duggan introduced historian John Bell to discuss his webpage, background, and book on the American Revolution.

items.title: Bell's Interest in the American Revolution
items.summary: Bell explained how growing up in Middlesex County during the Bicentennial and researching the death of Christopher Sider sparked his interest in lesser-known historical narratives.

items.title: The Powder Alarm and Provincial Congress
items.summary: Bell outlined how the 1774 Somerville Powder Alarm prompted Patriots to form a shadow provincial government and begin collecting cannons.

items.title: The Hunt for Stolen Artillery
items.summary: The speakers discussed why Royal Governor Thomas Gage prioritized recovering stolen colonial cannons over arresting prominent Patriot leaders.

items.title: Leslie's Retreat in Salem
items.summary: Bell recounted 'Leslie's Retreat' in February 1775, when British troops were blocked at a Salem drawbridge while searching for hidden weapons.

items.title: The Search at Barrett Farm
items.summary: Bell explained that the British marched to the Barrett Farm in Concord specifically because intelligence indicated the stolen Boston cannons were hidden there.

items.title: Paul Revere and the Medford Connection
items.summary: The speakers discussed Paul Revere's stop at the Isaac Hall House in Medford and the flight of local loyalist Isaac Royall.

items.title: The Structure of Colonial Militias
items.summary: Bell described how colonial militias were organized, trained, and quickly mobilized through structured local networks during emergencies.

items.title: Mechanics, Trains, and Henry Knox
items.summary: Bell defined historical terms like 'mechanics' and 'trains' and detailed how Henry Knox used militia service to elevate his social standing.

items.title: History of the 'Hancock' and 'Adams' Cannons
items.summary: Bell traced the postwar history of two recovered brass cannons that were displayed at the Bunker Hill Monument before being moved to museums.

items.title: The Boston Common Gun House Theft
items.summary: Bell detailed how Patriots stole two heavy cannons from a Boston Common gun house and hid them inside a school firewood chest directly under the noses of British guards.

items.title: The Exposure of Spy Benjamin Church
items.summary: Bell explained how a intercepted ciphered letter in late 1775 eventually proved that high-ranking Patriot Dr. Benjamin Church was spying for General Gage.

items.title: The Concord Spy and Medford Connection
items.summary: Bell identified merchant Duncan Ingraham as his top suspect for the Concord spy, noting his post-war move to Medford and election to the legislature.
